notes:
- **On a Mac, your agent can also use the apps you allow, not only websites.** It presses buttons
  and fills in boxes inside an app's window without moving your pointer, so you can keep working,
  and if you start using that app, it waits for you. Ask for it in the chat: the first time it
  needs an app, it asks you, and macOS asks you once to allow it. It never uses Terminal, password
  keepers, System Settings, Mail, Messages, Calendar, or your web browsers, it never types a
  password or a card you pay with, and anything it could not undo waits for you. On Windows, it
  uses websites.
- **Computer control is one list.** On the Connections tab, under Computer control, the websites
  and apps your agent can use sit in one list, with one Add box that takes a web address or an
  app's name.
- **You can see where your agent is working on a website.** A small Archie pointer moves to each
  button it presses in its browser window, and rests on the one it is asking you about, so the
  picture in your chat shows which button it means. Your own pointer is never touched.
- **Fixed two cases where your agent could do more on a website than you had allowed.**
- **Square Keeper** reads your live Square: what came in, who hasn't paid an invoice, and when your
  money lands. It drafts and sends invoices and refunds a payment, each shown to you before it goes.
- **Social Posting** posts to your Instagram, and to a Facebook Page if you have one. Send a photo
  and say what to say; it shows you the post and posts it when you say yes, now or at a time you
  pick.
- **Adding your own AI account takes less.** Archie tells which kind of account it is from what you
  paste, and every agent you made on the free credits starts using it right away.
- **A stopped agent's chat says so, with a Start button**, the way your phone shows it.
- **The Microsoft sign-in button says work or school account**, and the sign-in buttons look like
  Google's.
- **Your agent types a gift card, library card, loyalty, or membership number** when a site asks
  for one. A card you pay with is still always yours to type.
- **A text with a PIN in it is kept away from the AI**, the way a sign-in code already was.
